finding.claim: /checkout charges a total computed from client-supplied price and qty with no server-side price lookup or validation, so an authenticated customer can pay an arbitrary amount, including near-zero or negative totals (HIGH).
finding.source: req.body.items[].price and req.body.items[].qty in POST /checkout JSON body

trace.note: total = sum of i.price * i.qty from client body

finding.guards_checked: No server-side catalog price lookup on this route (contrast /checkout-v2 at cart.js:13). No validation of price or qty, no quantity cap, no finiteness or positivity check. Authentication is assumed via req.user but not enforced in this file; if the route is unauthenticated this escalates to CRITICAL. Payments implementation not in repo (negative-amount handling unknown).

verdict.guard_found: none. cart.js:5 sums client-supplied i.price * i.qty with no catalog lookup, validation, or bounds check, and cart.js:6 passes that total straight to req.payments.charge. The only other route, /checkout-v2 (cart.js:10-16), uses req.catalog.price and is not the route in the finding. No auth middleware, mount file, or payments implementation exists in the directory (only cart.js and .claude skill docs), so any guard would have to live outside the repo.
verdict.reason: POST /checkout at cart.js:4-7 charges a total computed entirely from req.body.items price and qty (cart.js:5) with nothing between that and req.payments.charge (cart.js:6), so any customer who can reach the route can set the charged amount. Whether the route requires login is not visible in this repo, but the attacker tier is at most an ordinary customer, so the finding stands; the trace matches the code at every cited line.

finding.claim: /checkout-v2 has no upper bound on qty and no finiteness check; Infinity (from JSON 1e400), NaN (non-numeric qty), or NaN from an unknown SKU can reach payments.charge (MEDIUM).
finding.source: req.body.items[].qty and req.body.items[].sku in POST /checkout-v2 JSON body

trace.note: catalog.price(i.sku) may return undefined for unknown SKU
total += p * Math.max(1, Math.floor(i.qty)); qty unbounded, NaN/Infinity propagate
payments.charge called with possibly non-finite total

finding.guards_checked: Server-side catalog price lookup present. Math.max(1, ...) clamps only the lower bound. No Number.isInteger check, no upper bound on qty, no finiteness check on p or total. Impact mostly confined to the attacker's own transaction, hence MEDIUM. Catalog and payments implementations not in repo.

verdict.guard_found: None in cart.js. The only control is Math.max(1, Math.floor(i.qty)) at cart.js:14, which clamps the lower bound only. Math.floor(NaN) stays NaN, Math.max(1, NaN) is NaN, and Math.max(1, Infinity) is Infinity, so non-finite values pass through. There is no Number.isInteger, upper-bound, or isFinite check on qty, and no check on p. The catalog.price result is used with no undefined check at cart.js:13-14. payments.charge at cart.js:16 is called with the unchecked total and its result is not verified in this file. Its implementation is not in the repo, so any validation there is unknown.
verdict.reason: The trace is accurate: cart.js:12-16 match the claim, and JSON 1e400 yields Infinity while an unknown SKU yields NaN through `p * ...`, so a non-finite total reaches payments.charge at cart.js:16 with no guard in this file. The attacker is any caller of POST /checkout-v2 (cart.js:10), with no role check in this file. Whether that is exploitable depends on how the unseen payments.charge handles NaN or Infinity, so the defect is confirmed but its severity is not.

finding.claim: Async handlers in /checkout and /checkout-v2 do not validate req.body.items; a missing or non-array items value throws inside an async Express handler. On Express 4 with Node 15+ this can be an unhandled rejection that terminates the process (MEDIUM; HIGH if unauthenticated).
finding.source: req.body.items in POST /checkout and POST /checkout-v2 (missing or non-array value)
finding.sink: Unhandled promise rejection from req.body.items.reduce (cart.js:5) and for...of req.body.items (cart.js:12)

trace.note: req.body.items.reduce throws TypeError when items is undefined or not an array
for...of throws TypeError when items is not iterable
async handler; no try/catch, rejection not forwarded to error middleware on Express 4

finding.guards_checked: No input validation on items, no try/catch, no error middleware in this file. Express version and any upstream middleware not in repo. Auth requirement unverified, which determines whether this is MEDIUM or HIGH.

verdict.guard_found: none in cart.js: no validation of req.body.items, no try/catch, no error middleware. Upstream auth, body-parser, and Express version are not in the repo.
verdict.reason: The trace is accurate: cart.js:5 calls req.body.items.reduce and cart.js:12 runs for...of over req.body.items with no guard, inside async handlers at cart.js:4 and cart.js:10. Whether this is reachable and whether it crashes the process cannot be decided from the repo. The code uses req.user.id at cart.js:6 and req.payments at cart.js:6 and cart.js:16, so upstream middleware must set them, but that middleware is not in the repo and it is unknown whether it requires auth. The process-termination claim also depends on the Express version (Express 4 does not forward async rejections), which is not in the repo.
